criterion: The home route changes visual register at a hard horizontal edge, from a saturated gradient ground to a plain white ground with near-black text.
evaluation_rule: The upper part of the home route sits on a magenta through red into yellow wash carrying white type; the part below it sits on a white ground with dark text. Yes if the change happens at a single hard edge with no gradual blend between the two. No if the two grounds blend into one another, or if only one of the two grounds appears on the route.

criterion: The featured model card at the head of the catalogue's latest column wears the same saturated gradient ground as the home hero.
evaluation_rule: The catalogue page carries one large featured card above a list of smaller cards. Yes if that featured card sits on the same magenta through red into yellow wash the home hero uses. No if the featured card sits on the plain white card ground every other card uses.

criterion: Every metadata line in the product, such as an owner handle or a run timestamp, is set in a mid grey that reads as subordinate to the black title above.
evaluation_rule: A metadata line is the secondary text under or beside a heading: an owner handle on a card, a date on a run row, a field type in a form. Yes if every such line is visibly lighter than the title it accompanies, in one consistent grey. No if a metadata line is the same weight and darkness as its title, or if two metadata lines use different greys.

criterion: A money warning, such as a spend limit notice or a standing cost line, is set in a dark amber on a pale yellow band.
evaluation_rule: A money warning is any message about spending: the monthly limit notice above the run form, or the per day cost beside a warm instance control. Yes if such a message sits on a pale yellow band with dark amber text. No if it uses the same red as a form error, or the same grey as ordinary body text.

criterion: On a wide screen the model page shows the run form in one column with the results panel in a second column beside that one.
evaluation_rule: Open a model page at a desktop width. Yes if the fields to fill in occupy one column and the results area occupies a second column beside them. No if the results area sits under the fields rather than beside them, or if the two share one column.

criterion: Every button, link, form control and tab in the product changes appearance when pointed at, when pressed, when focused by keyboard, and when unavailable.
evaluation_rule: Take any five interactive elements on the model page, the token screen and the catalogue. Yes if each one visibly differs at rest, under a pointer, while pressed, while focused from the keyboard, and while unavailable. No if any of the five looks identical at rest and under a pointer, or if an unavailable control is distinguished only by its colour.

criterion: Every symbol in the header, the badge row, the footer is drawn as vector geometry inside the page.
evaluation_rule: Look at the small symbols in the header, the badge row and the footer. Yes if each one is inline vector geometry that takes its colour from the text around it. No if any symbol is a loaded picture file or a glyph from an icon font.

criterion: Four regions stay put as a page scrolls: the top bar, the run control at the foot of the form column, the console side menu, the results panel.
evaluation_rule: Scroll a long model page and a long run history. Yes if the top bar, the run control, the console side menu and the results panel each remain visible while the content behind them moves. No if any of those four scrolls away with the content, or if a fifth region is pinned as well.

criterion: A card or panel waiting for its content shows a grey placeholder at the exact size the finished content will occupy.
evaluation_rule: Open the catalogue on a slow connection or throttle the network. Yes if each card that is still loading occupies its final footprint as a grey outline, so nothing on the page moves once the content lands. No if a turning spinner stands in for the content, or if the page shifts when the content arrives.

criterion: The keyboard focus indicator is drawn the same way everywhere, on the catalogue cards, the model page controls, the console rows alike.
evaluation_rule: Press tab through the catalogue, then through a model page, then through the run history. Yes if the indicator that appears is recognisably the same treatment on all three surfaces. No if one surface draws a different outline, or if one surface draws none at all.

criterion: A panel that reads as raised above the page is raised by a thin outline over a slightly whiter fill.
evaluation_rule: Look at a model card, a console table and a dialog on the white part of the site. Yes if each raised surface is separated from the page by a hairline outline over a marginally lighter fill. No if any of them casts a blurred shadow onto the page behind.

criterion: The generated artwork behind the company statement is three large soft coloured blobs drifting slowly across each other under a heavy blur.
evaluation_rule: Open the company statement surface. Yes if the artwork is a small number of large blurred colour masses whose positions change slowly over at least a minute. No if the artwork is a loaded picture, a sharp-edged pattern, or a still image that never moves.

criterion: A form rejected by the server nudges sideways by a barely visible amount before settling.
evaluation_rule: Submit the run form with a required field left empty. Yes if the form shifts a hair to one side then back, small enough to register as a refusal. No if the form jumps by a visible distance, or if the form makes no movement at all when the submission is rejected.

criterion: At phone width the run history, the token list and the usage list each read as a stack of self-contained cards rather than as a wide table squeezed sideways.
evaluation_rule: Open the run history, the token screen and the usage screen at phone width. Yes if each row reads as its own card, headed by the value that identifies it, with nothing cut off. No if any of the three keeps its columns and asks the reader to scroll sideways.

criterion: A claim cell on the home route carries a chart drawn from an invented figure when the real figure cannot be served.
evaluation_rule: The home route carries four claim cells, each pairing a sentence with a small chart of real platform figures. Yes if a cell renders a chart when its underlying figure is unavailable, so the drawing shows numbers nothing produced. No if such a cell renders its sentence with the chart area left out.
